Audit bundle: Full pre-registration sweep. I read the staged CSV, draft.json, curation.json, and found no existing comments.json. I used the cited Wikipedia source set first, then ran a bounded Wiki-family discovery pass. The discovery pass surfaced the same relevant Wiki-family candidate pages already represented by the source plan (History of architecture, List of architectural styles, per-style articles, per-building articles) plus optional broad pages such as Architectural style / Timeline of architectural styles; none materially changes the row universe, claim_type, or provenance story.

What passes:

1. Local table mechanics are clean.

- CSV shape is 16 rows × 4 columns, matching draft.json::columns.
- Primary key Architectural Style is unique across all 16 rows.
- CSV is alphabetically sorted by Architectural Style.
- source_count = 34 equals len(source_urls) = 34.
- Row count clears the 10-row gate.
- column_types cover all four columns and match the staged schema.
- query_category=qualitative with operation_type=projection is acceptable for this curator-selected exemplar table shape.
- domain=Culture/Architecture follows the current Family/Subdomain domain-taxonomy pattern and is not misleading.

2. Scope and claim_type are defensible.

The table is not source-defined and does not claim to be. The staged title and curation notes use selected / survey-canon / candidate_rebuild language, and the source set does not contain a closed authoritative Wikipedia mapping of architectural style -> single landmark building. That is the correct honesty level for this qualitative instance. The List of architectural styles article is broad and explicitly imperfect, but it is used as a candidate/style-context source rather than as a closed universe source. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_architectural_styles, lead and chronology sections, especially the style-definition lead and the incomplete-list notice; validation source-discovery result: no better Wiki-family closed mapping found.

3. Landmark/style grounding is adequate under the Landmark Rule.

The per-style pages support the staged landmark choices as canonical examples or highly visible exemplars, even though the single-exemplar choice remains curator judgment as declared. Spot-checks passed:

- Ancient Egyptian architecture -> Great Pyramid of Giza: the style article discusses the Giza necropolis and identifies the Great Pyramid of Giza / Pyramid of Khufu as a central pyramid example. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egyptian_architecture, Pyramid / Giza passage around lines 294-295.
- Mesoamerican architecture -> Pyramid of the Sun: the style article has a dedicated Pyramid of the Sun subsection and calls it the largest structure in Teotihuacan and one of the largest in the Western Hemisphere. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesoamerican_architecture, Pyramid of the Sun subsection around lines 216-223.
- Byzantine architecture -> Hagia Sophia: the style article calls Hagia Sophia the most famous example of Byzantine architecture and gives the 537 opening timeline. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byzantine_architecture, Hagia Sophia passage around lines 381-400.
- Japanese architecture -> Hōryū-ji: the style article names Hōryū-ji among the oldest surviving wooden buildings in Japan and shows it as an early Japanese architecture example. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Japanese_architecture, early Buddhist architecture passage around lines 223-233.
- Moorish architecture -> Alhambra: the style article uses Alhambra imagery in the lead and repeatedly cites Alhambra / Court of the Lions / Nasrid palaces as Moorish architectural examples. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moorish_architecture, lead image caption around lines 187-191 and Alhambra examples around lines 1146-1224.
- Mughal architecture -> Taj Mahal: the style article has a Taj Mahal subsection and gives construction 1632-1653. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mughal_architecture, Taj Mahal subsection around lines 340-345.
- Baroque architecture -> Palace of Versailles: the style article uses Hall of Mirrors / Palace of Versailles examples for French / Late Baroque. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baroque_architecture, France subsection around lines 384-398.
- Neoclassical architecture -> Brandenburg Gate: the style article uses Brandenburg Gate in the lead/example image set and names it with 1791. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture, lead/example passage around lines 186-188 and example around lines 450-452.
- Art Nouveau -> Casa Batlló: the Art Nouveau article lists Casa Batlló as a Gaudí example from 1904-1906. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Nouveau, Spain / Gaudí passage around lines 1104-1123.
- Art Deco -> Chrysler Building: the Art Deco article identifies Chrysler Building as completed in 1930 and discusses it as a major Art Deco skyscraper. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_Deco, New York skyscraper passage around lines 906-930.
- Modern architecture -> Villa Savoye: the Modern architecture article lists Villa Savoye and calls it a best-known / iconic modernist example. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_architecture, lead/examples and Le Corbusier passage around lines 212-214 and 391-419.

4. Per-building Country and Year cells are source-grounded.

Spot-checks across the 16 rows found the staged Modern-day Country and Year of Completion cells supported by the cited per-building pages:

- Great Pyramid of Giza: location Giza, Egypt; constructed c. 2600 BC. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Pyramid_of_Giza, infobox/lead around lines 302-334.
- Parthenon: Athens, Greece; Completed 432 BC. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parthenon, infobox around lines 275-282.
- Pantheon, Rome: Rome, Italy; Completed 126. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantheon,_Rome, infobox around lines 211-219.
- Pyramid of the Sun: Teotihuacan, Mexico State; Founded 200 AD. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyramid_of_the_Sun, infobox around lines 162-172.
- Hagia Sophia: Istanbul, Turkey; Completed 537 for the current structure. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagia_Sophia, infobox/lead around lines 308-347.
- Hōryū-ji: country Japan; Completed 607. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C5%8Dry%C5%AB-ji, infobox around lines 179-190. The 711 current-complex reconstruction caveat is documented in the staged notes and does not make 607 unsupported under the declared infobox-priority rule.
- Speyer Cathedral: Speyer, Germany; Speyer II completed in 1106. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speyer_Cathedral, location/country around lines 184-185 and Speyer II completion around lines 232-243.
- Notre-Dame de Paris: Paris, France; Completed 1345. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Notre-Dame_de_Paris, infobox around lines 263-280.
- Alhambra: Granada, Spain; Palace of the Lions / Muhammad V second reign 1362-1391 supports the staged 1391 latest-year convention. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alhambra, Nasrid / Court of the Lions passage around lines 304-309.
- Florence Cathedral: Florence, Italy; Completed 1436 except 19th century facade. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florence_Cathedral, infobox around lines 204-222.
- Taj Mahal: Agra, India; built 1631-1653 and complex completed in 1653. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal, infobox/lead around lines 296-344.
- Palace of Versailles: Versailles, France; construction phases from 1661 to 1715 support the staged 1715 completion convention. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palace_of_Versailles, infobox/lead around lines 265-281.
- Brandenburg Gate: Berlin, Germany; Completed 1791. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brandenburg_Gate, infobox/lead around lines 211-225.
- Casa Batlló: Barcelona, Spain; Gaudí renovation completed/refurbished in 1906. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Batll%C3%B3, infobox/body around lines 181-204 and 235-239.
- Chrysler Building: New York, US; Completed May 27, 1930. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chrysler_Building, infobox/lead around lines 231-278.
- Villa Savoye: Poissy, France; built between 1928 and 1931. Ground-truth source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Savoye, lead/infobox around lines 145-166.

Finding:

1. (structural, NON-BLOCKING HYGIENE) Year-source provenance prose overstates infobox extraction and has inconsistent Year-rule counts.

The CSV Year values are supported, but curation.json has current-state prose drift in the Year of Completion narrative:

- curation.json::normalization_decisions says "Direct-from-infobox cells (11 rows)" but the parenthetical list contains 12 rows: Parthenon, Pantheon, Hagia Sophia, Speyer Cathedral, Notre-Dame, Florence Cathedral, Taj Mahal, Brandenburg Gate, Casa Batlló, Chrysler Building, Villa Savoye, Hōryū-ji.
- The same paragraph says "Documented-exception cells (5 rows)" but enumerates only 4 rows: Great Pyramid of Giza, Pyramid of the Sun, Palace of Versailles, Alhambra. Hōryū-ji is described immediately after as infobox-priority, not as an exception.
- curation.json::source_coverage_notes says per-building articles provide "the infobox Completed year" for Year of Completion, with exceptions. Several correct staged cells are supported by article body or non-Completed infobox fields rather than by an infobox field literally named Completed: Speyer Cathedral 1106 is in the body as "Speyer II was completed in 1106" while its infobox shows Founded 1030 / Consecrated 1061 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speyer_Cathedral, lines 184-196 and 232-243); Casa Batlló 1906 is in the article body as completed/refurbished in 1906 rather than an infobox Completed field (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Casa_Batll%C3%B3, lines 181-204 and 235-239); Villa Savoye 1931 is supported by the lead/body "built between 1928 and 1931" rather than an infobox Completed field (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Villa_Savoye, lines 145-166).

Impact: non-blocking. This does not require a CSV repair because the Year cells are supported by the cited per-building pages and the Year Rule already allows ranges/approximate/documented exceptions. It is a provenance/narrative hygiene issue that could confuse a later auditor about whether all Year cells are infobox-exact.

Recommended repair: rewrite the source role and Year normalization prose to say "per-building articles provide the country and completion year via infobox Completed/Built fields or article-body completion statements, with documented range/approximation conventions." Then correct or remove the direct-from-infobox / documented-exception row counts. A simple safer wording is to avoid the two-count split and list only the rows requiring special interpretation: Great Pyramid (-2600), Pyramid of the Sun (200), Palace of Versailles (1715), Alhambra (1391), Hōryū-ji (607 infobox despite 711 current-complex caveat), plus optionally Speyer/Casa/Villa as body-supported rather than infobox-Completed.

Final judgment: Ready. The staged table is registration-ready under current benchmark policy because there are zero BLOCKING findings. The single finding is narrative/provenance hygiene only.

Minimal fixes needed before or after registration:
1. Clean the Year-source prose in source_coverage_notes and normalization_decisions.
2. Correct/remove the inconsistent direct-from-infobox and documented-exception counts.
